title: DELIVERY OF VINDHYAGIRI DESIG (Y3024) (PROJECT 17A INDIGENOUS ADVANCED STEALTH FRIGATE)
body_text: Vindhyagiri (Yard 3024), the seventh and final ship of Nilgiri class (Project 17A) and the third of the class built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd (GRSE), was delivered to the Indian Navy on 27 Nov 26 at GRSE, Kolkata, marking the successful culmination of Project 17A ship deliveries and a major milestone in achieving self-reliance in warship design and construction. Project 17A frigates are versatile multi-mission platforms, designed to address current and future challenges in the maritime domain. Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the ship is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate, that was part of the Indian Navy fleet from 08 Jul 1981 to 11 Jun 2012, rendering 31 years of glorious service to the nation. This state-of-the-art frigate reflects a quantum leap in naval design, stealth, firepower, automation and survivability and is an admirable symbol of Aatmanirbharta in warship building. Designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB) and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team (Kolkata), P17A frigates reflect a generational leap in indigenous ship design, stealth, survivability and combat capability. These ships feature an advanced suite of weapons and sensors compared to the P17 (Shivalik) class. The ships are configured with Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion plants, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine that drive a Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP) on each shaft, and a state-of-the-art Integrated Platform Management System (IPMS). The potent and technologically advanced weapons and sensors suite significantly enhances the ships’ multi-dimensional warfare capabilities across anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine domains. Delivery of Vindhyagiri marks a historic milestone wherein all seven P17A frigates have been delivered to the Indian Navy within a span of 23 months from the delivery of the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri) on 20 Dec 24 ( https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2086668 ). Furthermore, the institutional experience gained from the construction of preceding six P17A ships enabled a significant compression of the build period of Vindhyagiri to 68 months , in comparison to 84 months taken for the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri). Delivery of Vindhyagiri showcases the design, ship construction and engineering prowess of the nation and reflects Indian Navy’s unrelenting focus of Aatmanirbharta in both ship design and ship building. With an indigenisation content of 75%, the project has involved over 200 MSMEs and has enabled employment generation of approx. 4000 personnel directly and more than 10000 personnel indirectly . *** VM/SPS                                                                                                      255/26
